findings.body: Teardown attempts to delete a non-existent identity provider (NotFoundException) and, more importantly, the 20 created IDPs are never removed, leaking realm state into subsequent tests in the class/suite.
findings.failure_mode: Test teardown fails and/or leaves created identity providers behind, causing cross-test contamination.
findings.impact: Teardown attempts to delete a non-existent identity provider (NotFoundException) and, more importantly, the 20 created IDPs are never removed, leaking realm state into subsequent tests in the class/suite.
findings.root_cause: Hardcoded placeholder alias string in the cleanup registration instead of the alias actually used to create the provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the created alias in a final local (e.g. String alias = "idp-alias-" + i;) and register the cleanup with that alias: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);
findings.title: Test cleanup registers a non-existent IDP alias "alias"
findings.trigger: Running testCacheIDPForLogin: 20 providers are created with aliases idp-alias-0..idp-alias-19, but the cleanup task is registered for the literal alias "alias", which was never created; the task then runs in the test teardown.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 381 verbatim shows `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` inside a loop creating IDPs with aliases `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`. The cleanup registers literal string "alias" which was never created, so teardown will fail with NotFoundException and the 20 created IDPs leak.

pr.title: Add cache for IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin

raw_findings.body: Teardown attempts to delete a non-existent identity provider (NotFoundException) and, more importantly, the 20 created IDPs are never removed, leaking realm state into subsequent tests in the class/suite.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test teardown fails and/or leaves created identity providers behind, causing cross-test contamination.

raw_findings.root_cause: Hardcoded placeholder alias string in the cleanup registration instead of the alias actually used to create the provider.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Capture the created alias in a final local (e.g. String alias = "idp-alias-" + i;) and register the cleanup with that alias: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);
raw_findings.title: Test cleanup registers a non-existent IDP alias "alias"
raw_findings.trigger: Running testCacheIDPForLogin: 20 providers are created with aliases idp-alias-0..idp-alias-19, but the cleanup task is registered for the literal alias "alias", which was never created; the task then runs in the test teardown.

raw_findings.body: The provider idp-alias-20 (which by the end of the test is enabled, visible on login and linked to an organization) is never deleted, and teardown raises NotFoundException for the non-existent "alias" resource.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Teardown error and leaked organization-linked identity provider affecting subsequent tests.
raw_findings.impact: The provider idp-alias-20 (which by the end of the test is enabled, visible on login and linked to an organization) is never deleted, and teardown raises NotFoundException for the non-existent "alias" resource.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copy of the same hardcoded placeholder alias used in the loop above instead of the actual created alias.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Register the cleanup with the real alias: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove);
raw_findings.title: Second test cleanup also uses the placeholder alias "alias"
raw_findings.trigger: testCacheIDPForLogin creates the provider with alias "idp-alias-20" but registers cleanup for the alias "alias"; teardown executes the task.

raw_findings.body: No invalidation is registered although the IDP is still stored in the login caches; after the organization is re-enabled (which does not invalidate login caches either) the cached id set still contains the provider and the login page renders an IDP that is configured as hidden.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cache invalidation is skipped, leaving a stale getForLogin entry that returns a provider that no longer qualifies for login.
raw_findings.impact: No invalidation is registered although the IDP is still stored in the login caches; after the organization is re-enabled (which does not invalidate login caches either) the cached id set still contains the provider and the login page renders an IDP that is configured as hidden.
raw_findings.root_cause: The original model handed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() folds in organization state, making the eligibility comparison asymmetric with the raw updated model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the login predicate on the unwrapped original model (e.g. use idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()) for the comparison) so both sides of the comparison use the same, organization-state-independent semantics.
raw_findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update compares an organization-aware wrapper against a raw model
raw_findings.trigger: An IDP that is enabled, public and visible but linked to a currently *disabled* organization is present in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL id sets; an admin then updates it to set hideOnLogin=true. `idpById` comes from `getById(...)`, which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false while the organization is disabled, so getLoginPredicate().test(original) is false, and the updated raw model is also false, hitting the first early return.

raw_findings.body: An extra database query per identity-provider removal even when the cached CachedIdentityProvider already holds the model, adding avoidable load to bulk removals (e.g. realm/organization maintenance).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary DB round-trip on a code path that previously served entirely from cache.
raw_findings.impact: An extra database query per identity-provider removal even when the cached CachedIdentityProvider already holds the model, adding avoidable load to bulk removals (e.g. realm/organization maintenance).
raw_findings.root_cause: The delegate lookup was hoisted out of the isInvalid branch to make the model available for login invalidation, discarding the existing cache hit path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the model already available in the cache branch (cached.getIdentityProvider()) for registerIDPLoginInvalidation and only fall back to idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) when the cache entry is missing or invalidated.
raw_findings.title: remove() now issues an unconditional database lookup for every IDP removal
raw_findings.trigger: Any call to remove(alias) where the alias entry is already present in the realm cache (the previous else-branch path) now also hits the JPA delegate.

raw_findings.body: A regression that drops the invalidation calls added to create() and remove() would not be caught: the caches would stay populated with stale ids while the test still passes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Newly added invalidation logic in create()/remove() is unverified, so regressions ship undetected.
raw_findings.impact: A regression that drops the invalidation calls added to create() and remove() would not be caught: the caches would stay populated with stale ids while the test still passes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test only asserts the non-invalidating scenarios for create/remove, leaving the newly added registerIDPLoginInvalidation positive path untested.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend the test with a step that creates an enabled, non-hidden provider and a step that removes an enabled, non-hidden provider, asserting in each case that cacheKeyForLogin entries for all FetchMode values are null afterwards.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for login-cache invalidation on create/remove of a login-eligible IDP
raw_findings.trigger: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates a hidden provider and removes a disabled provider, i.e. only the false branch of registerIDPLoginInvalidation is exercised; the true branch (create/remove of an enabled, non-hidden provider) is never executed.

raw_findings.body: The predicate now also enforces an organization/BROKER_PUBLIC rule that is not represented by any LoginFilter constant nor by getLoginSearchOptions(), so the documented equivalence is wrong and callers building DB queries from getLoginSearchOptions() will get a wider result set than the predicate accepts.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale documentation misleads implementors of IdentityProviderStorageProvider into filtering differently in query and in-memory paths.
raw_findings.impact: The predicate now also enforces an organization/BROKER_PUBLIC rule that is not represented by any LoginFilter constant nor by getLoginSearchOptions(), so the documented equivalence is wrong and callers building DB queries from getLoginSearchOptions() will get a wider result set than the predicate accepts.
raw_findings.root_cause: An organization-specific condition was added inside LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() without updating the enum's contract documentation or its query-side counterpart.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the LoginFilter enum javadoc (and/or getLoginSearchOptions) to state that getLoginPredicate additionally requires organization-linked providers to be public brokers, or move the organization rule out of LoginFilter into a dedicated predicate.
raw_findings.title: LoginFilter javadoc/getLoginSearchOptions no longer describe all conditions applied by getLoginPredicate
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads the LoginFilter javadoc ("Enum that contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not") or uses getLoginSearchOptions() expecting it to be the query-side equivalent of getLoginPredicate().
